functions.name: LittleEndian::GET_WORD
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit value from the memory pointed to by ptr, interpreting the two bytes in little-endian order (least significant byte first), and returns it as mp_uword. Intended for parsing binary data with little-endian layout; independent of host endianness.
requirements: ptr must be non-null.
ptr must point to at least 2 readable bytes.
The memory region must be valid for reading and not be freed during the call.
Endianness is assumed to be little-endian in the source data; caller must only use it on buffers encoded as little-endian.
No error reporting is provided; caller must ensure bounds and validity before calling.

functions.name: LittleEndian::GET_DWORD
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit unsigned value from the memory pointed to by ptr, interpreting the four bytes in little-endian order, and returns it as mp_uint32. Use for parsing 32-bit fields from little-endian buffers; works regardless of host endianness.
requirements: ptr must be non-null.
ptr must point to at least 4 readable bytes.
The memory region must be valid for reading and not be freed during the call.
Endianness is assumed to be little-endian in the source data; caller must only use it on buffers encoded as little-endian.
No error reporting is provided; caller must ensure bounds and validity before calling.

requirements: ptr must be non-null.
ptr must point to at least 2 readable bytes.
The memory region must be valid for reading and not be freed during the call.

No error reporting is provided; caller must ensure bounds and validity before calling.

functions.name: BigEndian::GET_DWORD

requirements: ptr must be non-null.
ptr must point to at least 4 readable bytes.
The memory region must be valid for reading and not be freed during the call.

functions.name: XMFileBase::XMFileBase
functions.description: Default constructor for the abstract XMFileBase. Initializes internal state (e.g., base offset) for derived file implementations. Not directly usable on its own; instantiate a derived class such as XMFile.

functions.name: XMFileBase::~XMFileBase
functions.description: Virtual destructor to allow safe deletion through a XMFileBase pointer.

functions.name: XMFileBase::read
functions.signature: virtual mp_sint32 XMFileBase::read(void* ptr, mp_sint32 size, mp_sint32 count) = 0;
functions.description: Abstract read method. Reads up to count items of size bytes into the buffer pointed to by ptr from the current file position and advances the position accordingly. Returns the number of items successfully read.
requirements: ptr must point to a valid writable memory region of at least size*count bytes when count > 0.
size and count must be non-negative.
The file/stream must be open for reading.
The current position is advanced by the total number of bytes read (implementation-defined).
Callers must handle short reads (return value can be less than count).

functions.name: XMFileBase::write
functions.signature: virtual mp_sint32 XMFileBase::write(const void* ptr, mp_sint32 size, mp_sint32 count) = 0;
functions.description: Abstract write method. Writes up to count items of size bytes from the buffer pointed to by ptr to the current file position and advances the position accordingly. Returns the number of items successfully written.
requirements: ptr must point to a valid readable memory region of at least size*count bytes when count > 0.
size and count must be non-negative.
The file/stream must be open for writing.
Callers must handle short writes (return value can be less than count).

functions.name: XMFileBase::seek
functions.signature: virtual void XMFileBase::seek(mp_uint32 pos, SeekOffsetTypes seekOffsetType = SeekOffsetTypeStart) = 0;
functions.description: Abstract seek method. Moves the current file position relative to the specified origin (start, current, or end) by an offset of pos.
requirements: The file/stream must be open.
seekOffsetType must be one of SeekOffsetTypeStart, SeekOffsetTypeCurrent, or SeekOffsetTypeEnd.
pos is interpreted as an unsigned offset relative to the selected origin (exact bounds/overflow behavior are implementation-defined).

functions.name: XMFileBase::pos
functions.description: Abstract accessor returning the current file position as an unsigned byte offset from the beginning.
requirements: The file/stream should be open; behavior when closed is implementation-defined.

functions.name: XMFileBase::size
functions.description: Abstract accessor returning the total size of the file/stream in bytes.
requirements: The file/stream should be open; behavior when closed is implementation-defined.

functions.name: XMFileBase::isEOF
functions.description: Convenience method that reports end-of-file state. Returns true when pos() >= size().
requirements: Relies on pos() and size() to be valid for the underlying implementation.

functions.name: XMFileBase::getFileName
functions.description: Abstract accessor returning the file name/path as a system-character string (platform-dependent encoding).
requirements: Returned pointer must be treated as non-owning; lifetime/ownership are implementation-defined.

functions.name: XMFileBase::getFileNameASCII
functions.description: Abstract accessor returning the file name/path as an ASCII (char*) string.
requirements: Returned pointer must be treated as non-owning; lifetime/ownership are implementation-defined.

functions.name: XMFileBase::isOpen

functions.name: XMFileBase::isOpenForWriting

functions.name: XMFileBase::readByte
functions.description: Reads a single byte from the current position and advances the position by one byte. Thin wrapper around read(...).
requirements: The file/stream must be open for reading.
There must be at least 1 byte available; callers should check isEOF() before calling or handle implementation-defined behavior on EOF.

functions.name: XMFileBase::readWord
functions.description: Reads a word (mp_uword) from the current position and advances accordingly. Likely reads a fixed-width unsigned integer; exact width and byte order are determined by typedefs/implementation (unknown here).
requirements: The file/stream must be open for reading.
There must be at least sizeof(mp_uword) bytes available; callers should ensure not to read past EOF.
Endianness and alignment behavior are implementation-defined/unknown.

functions.name: XMFileBase::readDword
functions.description: Reads a double word (mp_dword) and advances the position. Exact width and byte order are defined by typedefs/implementation (unknown here).

functions.description: Reads count words (mp_uword elements) into buffer from the current position, advancing by count*sizeof(mp_uword). Wrapper around read(...).
requirements: buffer must point to a writable memory region of at least count*sizeof(mp_uword) bytes when count > 0.
count must be non-negative.
The file/stream must be open for reading.
Callers should handle short reads if the implementation returns fewer elements than requested (behavior not specified here).

functions.name: XMFileBase::readDwords
functions.description: Reads count double words (mp_dword elements) into buffer from the current position. Wrapper around read(...).
requirements: buffer must point to a writable memory region of at least count*sizeof(mp_dword) bytes when count > 0.
count must be non-negative.
The file/stream must be open for reading.
Callers should handle short reads if fewer elements are available (behavior not specified here).

functions.name: XMFileBase::writeByte
functions.description: Writes a single byte at the current position and advances by one byte. Wrapper around write(...).
requirements: The file/stream must be open for writing.

functions.name: XMFileBase::writeWord
functions.description: Writes a word (mp_uword) at the current position and advances accordingly. Exact width and byte order are implementation-defined (unknown here).

functions.name: TXMSample::getPaddedSize
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes to allocate for a sample buffer including TXMSample’s internal leading/trailing padding and bookkeeping.
requirements: Input size is the intended payload size in bytes (not including padding).
Return value must be used to size allocations when manually allocating compatible buffers.

functions.name: TXMSample::getPadStartAddr
functions.description: Given a pointer to the start of the usable (payload) sample buffer, returns the address to the beginning of the padded allocation (internal header at start).
requirements: Argument mem must be the exact pointer previously returned by TXMSample::allocPaddedMem or an equivalent padded layout.
Do not pass NULL.

functions.name: TXMSample::allocPaddedMem
functions.description: Allocates a sample buffer with TXMSample’s required internal padding and metadata. Returns a pointer to the start of the usable payload region of length ‘size’.
requirements: size is the payload size in bytes.
On success, the returned pointer must later be released with TXMSample::freePaddedMem.
The function zeroes the leading and trailing padding; the payload content is uninitialized.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check.

functions.name: TXMSample::freePaddedMem
functions.description: Frees a buffer previously allocated by TXMSample::allocPaddedMem. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: mem must be a pointer returned by TXMSample::allocPaddedMem or NULL.
Do not pass a pointer to the padded prolog (use the payload pointer).
After freeing, the pointer becomes invalid.

functions.name: TXMSample::copyPaddedMem
functions.signature: static void TXMSample::copyPaddedMem(void* dst, const void* src, mp_uint32 size)
functions.description: Copies a padded sample allocation, including TXMSample’s leading/trailing padding and metadata, from src to dst for a payload size of ‘size’.
requirements: dst and src must be payload pointers belonging to padded allocations laid out like TXMSample::allocPaddedMem.
size must be the payload size (in bytes) of the source/destination allocations.
The destination allocation must be at least TXMSample::getPaddedSize(size) bytes and already allocated.
Source and destination must not overlap.

functions.name: TXMSample::getSampleSizeInBytes
functions.description: Reads TXMSample’s internal metadata to report the payload size in bytes for the given padded sample payload pointer.
requirements: mem must be a valid payload pointer from TXMSample::allocPaddedMem.
Do not pass NULL.

functions.name: TXMSample::getSampleSizeInSamples
functions.description: Returns the number of samples in the buffer (accounts for 8-bit vs 16-bit based on internal state).
requirements: mem must be a valid payload pointer from TXMSample::allocPaddedMem.
Result uses internal bit-depth flag; caller should not assume bytes-per-sample without checking.

functions.name: TXMSample::smoothLooping
functions.description: Preprocesses the sample data to reduce clicks at loop boundaries using TXMSample’s double-buffering/padding scheme.
requirements: The object’s sample pointer and loop parameters must be initialized.
Callers modifying raw sample data should prefer setSampleValue and then call postProcessSamples when done.

functions.name: TXMSample::restoreOriginalState
functions.description: Restores the sample buffer to its original state if it has been smoothed or otherwise altered by the loop-double-buffer mechanism.
requirements: The TXMSample instance must have been initialized; no arguments.
Safe usage assumes the object tracks its original data in the padded region.

functions.name: TXMSample::postProcessSamples
functions.description: Updates loop-related buffered regions after direct sample modifications to maintain smooth looping playback.
requirements: Call after changing loop information or after using setSampleValue/getSampleValue to modify raw data, per header comment.
The TXMSample instance must have valid sample/loop fields.

functions.name: TXMSample::getSampleValue
functions.description: Returns the sample value at the given index from this TXMSample’s buffer. Range depends on bit depth: [-32768, 32767] for 16-bit, [-128, 127] for 8-bit.
requirements: index must be within the sample length (implementation uses object’s size/bit-depth).
TXMSample::sample must be non-NULL and point to a padded allocation.

functions.name: TXMSample::setSampleValue
functions.description: Writes a sample value at index into this TXMSample’s buffer, clamped to the valid range for the bit depth.
requirements: index must be within the sample length.
Value must fit the bit depth: 8-bit [-128,127], 16-bit [-32768,32767] (caller should respect these ranges).
Call TXMSample::postProcessSamples after a batch of modifications to update loop-buffer areas.

requirements: dest must point to a buffer large enough to hold the compressed pattern (exact size depends on data; not specified here).
The TXMPattern instance must have valid patternData and related fields (rows, channum, len).

functions.name: TXMPattern::decompress
functions.description: Decompresses a pattern from the given source buffer of length len into this pattern’s patternData. Returns the number of bytes consumed or a negative error code.
requirements: src must point to a buffer with at least len bytes.
TXMPattern must have storage/metadata ready to receive decompressed data (implementation-specific).

functions.name: XModule::loadModuleSample
functions.signature: mp_sint32 XModule::loadModuleSample(XMFileBase& f, mp_sint32 index, mp_sint32 flags8 = ST_DEFAULT, mp_sint32 flags16 = ST_16BIT, mp_uint32 alternateSize = 0)
functions.description: Loads a single sample (by index) for the current module from the file, using 8-bit/16-bit decoding flags as appropriate. Returns non-negative on success, negative on error.
requirements: index must refer to a valid sample slot in the module (0..MP_MAXSAMPLES-1).
f must be a valid, open XMFileBase positioned for this sample’s data.
flags8/flags16 are combinations of ST_* flags for 8/16-bit samples.
If alternateSize is non-zero, it may override expected sample size (implementation-specific).

functions.name: XModule::loadModuleSamples
functions.signature: mp_sint32 XModule::loadModuleSamples(XMFileBase& f, mp_sint32 flags8 = ST_DEFAULT, mp_sint32 flags16 = ST_16BIT)
functions.description: Loads all samples for the current module from the file using the provided 8-bit/16-bit decoding flags. Returns a status code (non-negative on success).
requirements: f must be valid and positioned according to the module format loaders.
flags8/flags16 are combinations of ST_* flags.
The module’s sample descriptors must be initialized before calling.

functions.name: XModule::convertXMVolumeEffects
functions.signature: static void XModule::convertXMVolumeEffects(mp_ubyte volume, mp_ubyte& eff, mp_ubyte& op)
functions.description: Converts an XM volume column byte into a standard effect type (eff) and operand (op).
requirements: eff and op must be references to variables that can be assigned.
volume is an XM volume column value (0..255).

functions.name: XModule::allocSampleMem
functions.description: Allocates sample memory from the module’s internal sample pool. Memory is padded at the start and end (documented as 16 bytes each) to aid interpolation/looping.
requirements: size is the requested payload size in bytes.
Returned pointer must be freed with XModule::freeSampleMem.
May return NULL if allocation or pool insertion fails; caller must check.
Only use this for module-owned samples managed by XModule.

functions.name: XModule::freeSampleMem
functions.signature: void XModule::freeSampleMem(mp_ubyte* mem, bool assertCheck = true)
functions.description: Frees sample memory previously allocated via XModule::allocSampleMem and removes it from the module’s pool. Safe handling of NULL is not explicitly stated; follow implementation.
requirements: mem must have been returned by XModule::allocSampleMem for this XModule instance.
assertCheck controls internal assertion behavior when freeing unexpected pointers (implementation-specific).
Do not free memory twice.

functions.name: XModule::cleanUp
functions.description: Resets/cleans the module state prior to loading a song; releases resources such as samples and clears structures.
requirements: Should be called before loading a new song, per comment.
After cleanup, previous pointers and indices should be considered invalid.

functions.name: XModule::postProcessSamples
functions.description: Iterates through samples and performs post-processing to avoid interpolation clicks; heavy=true may perform more expensive processing.
requirements: The module must have its samples loaded/initialized.
This may be time-consuming when heavy is true.

functions.name: XModule::setDefaultPanning
functions.description: Initializes default panning for channels/samples according to the module’s conventions.
requirements: Call after creating or loading a song if default panning is needed.
No parameters; operates on module state.

functions.name: XModule::addVolumeEnvelope
functions.description: Adds a volume envelope to the module’s envelope list, expanding storage as needed.
requirements: env must contain valid envelope points per TEnvelope semantics.
Number of envelopes maintained must match header.venvnum for consistency.

functions.name: XModule::addPanningEnvelope
functions.description: Adds a panning envelope to the module’s envelope list, expanding storage as needed.
requirements: env must be valid by TEnvelope rules.
Consistency with header.penvnum is expected.

functions.name: XModule::addFrequencyEnvelope
functions.description: Adds a frequency envelope to the module’s envelope list, expanding storage as needed.
requirements: env must be valid by TEnvelope rules.
Consistency with header.fenvnum is expected.

functions.name: XModule::addVibratoEnvelope
functions.description: Adds a vibrato envelope to the module’s envelope list, expanding storage as needed.
requirements: env must be valid by TEnvelope rules.
Consistency with header.vibenvnum is expected.

functions.name: XModule::addPitchEnvelope
functions.description: Adds a pitch envelope to the module’s envelope list, expanding storage as needed.
requirements: env must be valid by TEnvelope rules.
Consistency with header.pitchenvnum is expected.

functions.name: XModule::vol64to255
functions.description: Converts a volume from [0..64] scale to [0..255] scale with rounding.
requirements: Input vol should be in [0,64]; values >64 are clamped.

functions.name: XModule::vol255to64
functions.description: Converts a volume from [0..255] scale to [0..64] scale using integer scaling.
requirements: Input vol should be in [0,255].

functions.name: XModule::vol127to255
functions.description: Converts a volume from [0..127] to [0..255] scale with rounding.
requirements: Input vol should be in [0,127]; values >127 are clamped.

functions.name: XModule::vol128to255
functions.description: Converts a volume from [0..128] to [0..255] scale with rounding.
requirements: Input vol should be in [0,128]; values >128 are clamped.

functions.name: XModule::pan15to255
functions.description: Converts a 4-bit panning value [0..15] to [0..255] by scaling (pan>=0xF maps to 0xFF).
requirements: Input pan should be in [0,15].

functions.name: XModule::XModule
functions.description: Constructs an XModule instance and allocates/initializes internal structures for song data and loader management.
requirements: None beyond standard construction; heavy allocations may occur during later operations.

functions.name: XModule::~XModule
functions.description: Destructor; releases resources owned by the XModule, including sample memory and allocated structures.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.

functions.name: XModule::getType
functions.description: Returns the detected/assigned module type for this XModule instance.
requirements: Valid after identification or loading; default may be ModuleType_UNKNOWN.

functions.name: XModule::identifyModule
functions.signature: static const char* XModule::identifyModule(const mp_ubyte* buffer)
functions.description: Runs registered loaders’ identification on the given header bytes and returns an identifier string or NULL if unrecognized.
requirements: buffer must contain exactly XModule::IdentificationBufferSize bytes from the start of the file (per comment).
Return pointer is a c-string owned by the loader; treat as read-only and possibly transient.

functions.name: XModule::loadModule
functions.signature: mp_sint32 XModule::loadModule(XMFileBase& f, bool scanForSubSongs = false)
functions.description: Loads a module from an already-open file handle using the appropriate loader. Optionally scans for subsongs. Returns a status code (non-negative on success).
requirements: f must be valid and positioned at file start unless loaders handle otherwise.
Call cleanUp() before loading a new song.
If scanForSubSongs is true, expect longer load time.

functions.name: XModule::saveExtendedModule
functions.signature: mp_sint32 XModule::saveExtendedModule(const SYSCHAR* fileName, const char* trackerString = NULL)
functions.description: Exports the module in FastTracker 2 (.XM) extended format. Returns a status code.
requirements: fileName must be a valid writable path.
Optional trackerString may be NULL or a c-string to embed as tracker info.
Module must be in a consistent state; exporter depends on module content.

functions.name: XModule::saveProtrackerModule
functions.description: Exports the module in ProTracker-compatible (.MOD) format. Returns a status code.
requirements: fileName must be a valid writable path.
Module content must satisfy format limits (channels, instruments, features).

functions.name: XModule::isModuleLoaded
functions.description: Indicates whether a module is currently loaded into this XModule instance.
requirements: None.

functions.name: XModule::convertStr
functions.signature: static void XModule::convertStr(char* strIn, const char* strOut, mp_sint32 nLen, bool filter = true)
functions.description: Converts/copies string data between module and host encoding, optionally filtering characters. Naming suggests strIn is destination and strOut is source (but parameter names are ambiguous).
requirements: strIn must point to a writable buffer with at least nLen bytes.
strOut must point to at least nLen bytes of readable input.
If filter is true, the function may sanitize characters. Details are not specified in the header.

functions.name: XModule::getTitle
functions.signature: void XModule::getTitle(char* str, bool filter = true) const
functions.description: Retrieves the module title into the provided buffer, optionally filtering characters.
requirements: str must point to a writable buffer large enough for the title (recommend at least MP_MAXTEXT bytes).

functions.name: XModule::getSignature
functions.signature: void XModule::getSignature(char* str, bool filter = true) const
functions.description: Retrieves the module file signature into the provided buffer, optionally filtering characters.
requirements: str must be a writable buffer sufficiently large (recommend at least MP_MAXTEXT bytes).

functions.name: XModule::getTracker
functions.signature: void XModule::getTracker(char* str, bool filter = true) const
functions.description: Retrieves the tracker name string into the provided buffer, optionally filtering characters.
requirements: str must be a writable buffer sufficiently large (recommend at least MP_MAXTEXT bytes).

functions.name: XModule::allocateSongMessage
functions.description: Allocates an empty song message buffer with an initial capacity.
requirements: initialSize is the initial capacity in bytes for the song message.
Call before adding lines via addSongMessageLine if no message exists.

functions.name: XModule::addSongMessageLine
functions.description: Appends one text line to the song message.
requirements: line must be a valid null-terminated c-string.
allocateSongMessage must have been called or a message buffer must already exist.

functions.name: XModule::getFirstSongMessageLineLength
functions.description: Initializes iteration over song message lines and returns the length of the first line, or a sentinel value if none.
requirements: Call this before getNextSongMessageLineLength/getSongMessageLine to start iteration.

functions.name: XModule::getNextSongMessageLineLength
functions.description: Continues iteration over song message lines; returns the length of the next line, or a sentinel value if no more.
requirements: Must be called after getFirstSongMessageLineLength and while iterating lines.

functions.name: XModule::getSongMessageLine
functions.description: Copies the current iterated song message line into the provided buffer.
requirements: line must be a writable buffer large enough for the current line including terminator.
Must be called after requesting a line length with getFirst/NextSongMessageLineLength.

functions.name: XModule::buildSubSongTable
functions.description: Analyzes orders/patterns to populate the internal sub-song table for modules containing multiple subsongs.
requirements: Call after loading or creating the module before using subsong accessors.

functions.name: XModule::getNumSubSongs
functions.description: Returns the number of detected sub-songs.
requirements: Call after buildSubSongTable for up-to-date results.

functions.name: XModule::getSubSongPosStart
functions.description: Returns the starting order index for subsong i.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getNumSubSongs()-1].
buildSubSongTable should have been called.

functions.name: XModule::getSubSongPosEnd
functions.description: Returns the ending order index (inclusive or exclusive depending on implementation) for subsong i.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getNumSubSongs()-1].
buildSubSongTable should have been called.
Inclusive/exclusive nature is not specified here.

functions.name: XModule::removeOrderSkips
functions.description: Scans the order list and removes unused skip markers (0xFE orders).
requirements: Module orders must be loaded/initialized.
Operation mutates the order list.

functions.name: XModule::removeUnusedPatterns
functions.description: Removes patterns that are not referenced by any order. If evaluate is true, may only analyze or report without removal (implementation-specific). Returns a count/status.
requirements: Patterns and order list must be initialized.
Behavior for evaluate=true is not fully specified in header.

functions.name: XModule::getNumUsedPatterns
functions.description: Returns the number of patterns that are referenced/used in the current module.
requirements: Orders/patterns must be available.

functions.name: XModule::getNumUsedInstruments
functions.description: Returns the number of instruments that are actually referenced/used by the module.
requirements: Instruments and patterns must be available.

functions.name: XModule::postLoadAnalyser
functions.description: Analyzes the loaded module for format-specific quirks (e.g., ProTracker instrument change behavior) and sets module flags accordingly.
requirements: Call after successfully loading a module.

functions.name: XModule::createEmptySong
functions.signature: void XModule::createEmptySong(bool clearPatterns = true, bool clearInstruments = true, mp_sint32 numChannels = 8)
functions.description: Initializes the module as an empty song, optionally clearing patterns and instruments and setting the number of channels.
requirements: numChannels should be a positive integer supported by the tracker.
If clear flags are false, existing data may persist.

functions.name: XModule::isPTCompatible
functions.description: Checks whether the module can be exported as a ProTracker-compatible MOD and returns an error code explaining incompatibilities if any.
requirements: Call after module is populated.
Caller must handle non-zero error codes as incompatibility indicators.

functions.name: XModule::LoaderInterface::~LoaderInterface
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the loader interface to allow proper cleanup via base pointers.
requirements: Implementations should ensure derived resources are released.

functions.name: XModule::LoaderInterface::identifyModule
functions.description: Pure virtual; returns a c-string identifying the module format if recognized based on the header buffer, or NULL otherwise.
requirements: buffer must contain XModule::IdentificationBufferSize bytes from the start of the file (per comment).
Implementations must not modify the buffer and should return stable strings or document ownership.

functions.name: XModule::LoaderInterface::load
functions.description: Pure virtual; attempts to load a module from f into module. Returns a status code (non-negative success, negative error).
requirements: f must be a valid, open file abstraction positioned as required by the loader.
module must be a valid pointer to an XModule to populate.
identifyModule should be called and succeed before load.

functions.name: XModule::SampleLoader::SampleLoader
functions.description: Constructs a SampleLoader bound to a file stream for reading sample data.
requirements: file must refer to a valid XMFileBase instance whose lifetime exceeds the SampleLoader’s.

functions.name: XModule::SampleLoader::~SampleLoader
functions.description: Virtual destructor for SampleLoader implementations.
requirements: Derived classes should release resources here.

functions.name: XModule::SampleLoader::load_sample_8bits
functions.signature: virtual mp_sint32 XModule::SampleLoader::load_sample_8bits(void* p_dest_buffer, mp_sint32 compressedSize, mp_sint32 p_buffsize) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual; loads/decodes an 8-bit sample into p_dest_buffer from the underlying file. Returns number of bytes written or a status code.
requirements: p_dest_buffer must point to writable memory of at least p_buffsize bytes.
compressedSize is the size of the encoded sample data (format-specific).
Implementations must not overflow the destination buffer.

functions.name: XModule::SampleLoader::load_sample_16bits
functions.signature: virtual mp_sint32 XModule::SampleLoader::load_sample_16bits(void* p_dest_buffer, mp_sint32 compressedSize, mp_sint32 p_buffsize) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual; loads/decodes a 16-bit sample into p_dest_buffer from the underlying file. Returns number of bytes written or a status code.
requirements: p_dest_buffer must point to writable memory of at least p_buffsize bytes.
compressedSize is the size of the encoded sample data (format-specific).
Implementations must respect endianness and not overflow the destination buffer.

functions.name: AudioDriverManager::AudioDriverManager
functions.description: Constructor for the AudioDriverManager. Initializes internal state used to provide and manage AudioDriverInterface instances and to enumerate available drivers. Specific initialization details are not documented in this header.
requirements: The object must be successfully constructed before calling any other member functions.
Ensure sufficient memory is available for construction; behavior on allocation failure is implementation-defined/unknown.
Use the matching destructor to release any resources when done (RAII).

functions.name: AudioDriverManager::~AudioDriverManager
functions.description: Destructor for the AudioDriverManager. Releases any resources held by the manager, including internally stored driver lists and enumeration state. Exact cleanup/ownership semantics are not documented here.
requirements: Do not access the object or any of its resources after destruction.
Ensure the destructor is invoked exactly once per constructed instance (automatically handled for automatic objects).
If any AudioDriverInterface pointers returned by this manager have ownership/cleanup requirements, follow those per their own documentation (ownership is unknown from this header).

functions.name: AudioDriverManager::getPreferredAudioDriver
functions.description: Returns the preferred audio driver for the current system as an AudioDriverInterface pointer. Returns NULL if none is available or if an allocation error occurred. Ownership and lifetime of the returned pointer are not specified in this header.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL before dereferencing or using the driver.
Only call on a valid, constructed AudioDriverManager instance.
Thread-safety/recursion guarantees are not documented; avoid concurrent calls unless implementation states otherwise.
Follow AudioDriverInterface-specific requirements for subsequent use and potential release of the returned driver (ownership unknown).

functions.name: AudioDriverManager::getAudioDriverByName
functions.description: Looks up and returns an AudioDriverInterface by the given driver name. If no matching driver exists or an allocation/lookup error occurs, the function likely returns NULL (not explicitly documented). Ownership of the returned pointer is not specified in this header.
requirements: The name parameter must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer (non-NULL).
Caller should check the return value for NULL before use (inferred due to typical lookup semantics; exact behavior not documented).
Only call on a valid, constructed AudioDriverManager instance.
Follow AudioDriverInterface-specific requirements for using and possibly releasing the returned driver (ownership unknown).

functions.name: AudioDriverManager::getFirstDriverName
functions.description: Begins enumeration of available audio driver names and returns the first driver's name as a const C string, or possibly NULL if no drivers are available (not explicitly documented). Intended to be used with getNextDriverName() to iterate. The returned string should be treated as read-only; lifetime/ownership of the pointer are not specified.
requirements: Call this function to start a new enumeration sequence before calling getNextDriverName().
Treat the returned string as read-only; do not modify or free it.
Caller should check for a NULL return to detect absence of drivers (inferred; not explicitly documented).
Only call on a valid, constructed AudioDriverManager instance and ensure the instance remains alive while using returned pointers.

functions.name: AudioDriverManager::getNextDriverName
functions.description: Continues enumeration of available audio driver names and returns the next driver's name as a const C string, or possibly NULL when enumeration is complete (not explicitly documented). Used after getFirstDriverName(). Returned string should be treated as read-only; lifetime/ownership are not specified.
requirements: Call getFirstDriverName() before the first call to this function in an enumeration sequence.
Treat the returned string as read-only; do not modify or free it.
Caller should check for a NULL return to detect end of enumeration (inferred; not explicitly documented).
Only call on a valid, constructed AudioDriverManager instance and ensure the instance remains alive while using returned pointers.

functions.name: AudioDriverManager::getPreferredAudioDriverSampleRate
functions.description: Returns the preferred audio driver sample rate for the system. The unit is presumably Hertz, but the exact unit and valid value range are not documented here. Behavior when no preferred value exists is not specified.
requirements: Only call on a valid, constructed AudioDriverManager instance.
Caller should be prepared to handle any mp_sint32 value, including potential sentinel or non-positive values indicating an unknown/unsupported rate (inferred; not explicitly documented).

functions.name: AudioDriverManager::getPreferredAudioDriverBufferSize
functions.description: Returns the preferred audio driver buffer size for the system. The unit (frames, samples, or bytes) and valid range are not documented in this header. Behavior when no preferred value exists is not specified.
requirements: Only call on a valid, constructed AudioDriverManager instance.
Caller should be prepared to handle any mp_sint32 value, including potential sentinel or non-positive values indicating an unknown/unsupported size (inferred; not explicitly documented).

functions.name: MasterMixer::MasterMixer
functions.signature: MasterMixer::MasterMixer(mp_uint32 sampleRate, mp_uint32 bufferSize = 0, mp_uint32 numDevices = 1, class AudioDriverInterface* audioDriver = 0)
functions.description: Constructs a MasterMixer with the given sample rate, optional buffer size, number of devices it can handle, and an optional audio driver interface. Intended to set up the mixer state prior to opening/starting audio. Details about initial internal states (initialized/started/paused) and error reporting are not documented in this header.
requirements: sampleRate is expected to be a valid audio sample rate (exact valid range unknown).
If provided, audioDriver must point to a valid AudioDriverInterface instance or be null.
numDevices should be a positive count of mixable devices (exact constraints unknown).
bufferSize may be 0 to let the mixer/driver choose (behavior unspecified); other constraints on size are unknown.

functions.name: MasterMixer::~MasterMixer
functions.description: Destructor for MasterMixer. Cleans up resources associated with the mixer (e.g., allocated buffers, audio driver handles) upon object destruction. Specific teardown order or side effects are not documented here.
requirements: Must not be called while external audio threads are using the object; ensure playback is stopped and devices are closed before destruction (inferred best practice).

functions.name: MasterMixer::setMasterMixerNotificationListener
functions.description: Registers a listener object to receive mixer notifications (e.g., buffer size or sample rate changes). Pass nullptr to clear. The listener's masterMixerNotification will be called on relevant events.
requirements: listener must remain valid for as long as it is registered, or be unset before destruction.
Listener implementation must be thread-safe if notifications can occur from an audio callback thread (threading context unspecified).

functions.name: MasterMixer::openAudioDevice
functions.description: Opens/initializes the underlying audio device/driver for subsequent start/resume operations. Returns a status code; exact semantics are not documented.
requirements: Must be called before start() to begin playback (inferred).
May require a valid audio driver configured, either via constructor or setCurrentAudioDriverByName (inferred).

functions.name: MasterMixer::closeAudioDevice
functions.description: Closes/releases the underlying audio device/driver. Returns a status code; exact success/error codes are not documented.
requirements: Should be called after stopping playback (inferred).
After closing, mixer cannot play until openAudioDevice() is called again (inferred).

functions.name: MasterMixer::start
functions.description: Starts audio playback/processing for the mixer. Returns a status code; details not specified. Sets the mixer to a started state if successful.
requirements: Audio device should be successfully opened before calling (inferred).
Should not be called if already started unless the implementation supports idempotency (behavior unspecified).

functions.name: MasterMixer::stop
functions.description: Stops audio playback/processing for the mixer. Returns a status code; exact values not specified. Transitions the mixer out of the started state.
requirements: If audio is playing, call stop() before closeAudioDevice() (inferred).
Safe reentrancy or repeated calls are not documented.

functions.name: MasterMixer::pause
functions.description: Pauses audio playback without fully stopping the device. Returns a status code; details not specified. Sets the paused state internally upon success.
requirements: Should only be called when playback has been started (inferred).

functions.name: MasterMixer::resume
functions.description: Resumes audio playback after a pause. Returns a status code; details not specified. Clears the paused state upon success.
requirements: Should be called after a successful pause() (inferred).

functions.name: MasterMixer::isPlaying
functions.description: Returns true if the mixer has been started (regardless of paused state). Convenience status query.

functions.name: MasterMixer::isPaused
functions.description: Returns true if the mixer is currently paused. Convenience status query.

functions.name: MasterMixer::isInitialized
functions.description: Returns true if the mixer (and likely its audio device/driver) has been initialized. Exact conditions for initialization are not documented.

functions.name: MasterMixer::isActive
functions.description: Returns true if the mixer is started and not paused (actively producing audio). Convenience status query.

functions.name: MasterMixer::setBufferSize
functions.description: Sets the mixer/audio buffer size in samples or frames (unit not specified). May trigger a notification to the registered listener. Returns a status code; exact semantics unknown.
requirements: bufferSize must be a valid non-negative size; whether zero is allowed here is unspecified.
May need to be called before opening/starting the audio device for effect; runtime reconfiguration behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: MasterMixer::getBufferSize
functions.description: Returns the current buffer size used by the mixer/audio driver. Unit (samples/frames) is not specified.

functions.name: MasterMixer::setSampleRate
functions.description: Sets the mixer output sample rate. May trigger a notification to the registered listener. Returns a status code; exact semantics unknown.
requirements: sampleRate should be a valid audio rate (e.g., 44100, 48000); exact accepted values are unspecified.
Changing sample rate during playback may have constraints; unspecified in this header.

functions.name: MasterMixer::getSampleRate
functions.description: Returns the current output sample rate of the mixer.

functions.name: MasterMixer::addDevice
functions.signature: bool MasterMixer::addDevice(Mixable* device, bool paused = false)
functions.description: Adds a Mixable device (sound source/effect) to the mixer. Optionally adds it initially paused. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: device must be a valid, initialized Mixable pointer and must remain valid while managed by the mixer.
Must not add the same device multiple times unless supported (unspecified).
If paused is true, the device will be added in a paused state.

functions.name: MasterMixer::removeDevice
functions.signature: bool MasterMixer::removeDevice(Mixable* device, bool blocking = true)
functions.description: Schedules or performs removal of a Mixable device from the mixer. If blocking is true, the removal may wait until it is safe to detach. Returns true on success.
requirements: device must be a Mixable previously added to the mixer.
If blocking is true, the caller must tolerate potential blocking/wait (e.g., until audio callback reaches a safe point). Exact threading/latency behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: MasterMixer::isDeviceRemoved
functions.description: Checks whether a previously managed Mixable device has been removed (or marked and completed removal). Returns true if it is no longer active within the mixer.
requirements: device should be a valid pointer to a Mixable formerly or currently managed by the mixer.

functions.name: MasterMixer::pauseDevice
functions.signature: bool MasterMixer::pauseDevice(Mixable* device, bool blocking = true)
functions.description: Pauses an individual Mixable device within the mixer. If blocking is true, may wait for a safe point to apply the pause. Returns true on success.
requirements: device must refer to a Mixable currently added to the mixer.
If blocking is true, the call may block; caller must be prepared for potential latency.

functions.name: MasterMixer::resumeDevice
functions.description: Resumes a previously paused Mixable device. Returns true on success.
requirements: device must refer to a Mixable currently added to the mixer.
The device should have been paused before calling resumeDevice (inferred).

functions.name: MasterMixer::isDevicePaused
functions.description: Queries whether a Mixable device managed by the mixer is currently paused. Returns true if paused.
requirements: device must refer to a Mixable that is or was managed by the mixer.

functions.name: MasterMixer::mixerHandler
functions.description: Audio callback/mix function that fills or processes the provided output buffer with mixed audio from attached devices, applying optional filter hooks and limiting. Intended to be called by the audio driver with the appropriate buffer.
requirements: buffer must be a valid writable pointer to an output buffer with capacity for the mix operation; required length/format are not specified in the header.
Should only be called while the mixer is initialized and started (inferred).
Threading context is likely an audio callback; the function should be considered real-time safe by callers (inferred).

functions.name: MasterMixer::setSampleShift
functions.description: Controls output loudness by right-shifting sample values by 'shift' bits (i.e., divide by 2^shift). Larger shift reduces volume. Intended for simple attenuation.
requirements: shift represents a right bit-shift; negative values would imply left shift, but behavior for negatives is unspecified.
Caller should avoid excessive shift values that could mute output; exact safe range is unspecified.

functions.name: MasterMixer::getSampleShift
functions.description: Returns the current sample right-shift value used for output attenuation.

functions.name: MasterMixer::setDisableMixing
functions.description: Globally disables mixing when set to true. Intended for special/legacy scenarios; comment suggests typical users need not use this.

functions.name: MasterMixer::setFilterHook
functions.description: Sets a filter hook Mixable that can post-process the mixed signal. Acts as an insert/processing stage for the master output.
requirements: filterHook must be a valid Mixable or nullptr; lifetime must exceed its use by the mixer.

functions.name: MasterMixer::getFilterHook
functions.description: Returns the provided filterHook argument unchanged. Note: This appears to be a likely header bug; a typical getter should take no arguments and return the internally stored filter hook. As declared/defined here, it echoes its input value.
requirements: Callers should not rely on this to retrieve the internally set filter hook because, as declared, it ignores internal state and returns the argument passed in.

functions.name: MasterMixer::getAudioDriver
functions.description: Returns the current AudioDriverInterface in use by the mixer, if any.

functions.name: MasterMixer::getCurrentAudioDriverName
functions.description: Returns the name of the currently selected audio driver as a C string. Exact lifetime/ownership of the returned string is unspecified.

functions.name: MasterMixer::setCurrentAudioDriverByName
functions.description: Selects the current audio driver by name. Returns true on success. Useful for switching output backends.
requirements: name must point to a valid, null-terminated C string representing a driver name.
May only be called when audio is stopped/closed; hot-switching behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: MasterMixer::getAudioDriverManager
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the AudioDriverManager associated with the mixer, if any.

functions.name: MasterMixer::getCurrentSample
functions.description: Retrieves a current sample value at the given position and channel from the master stream, likely for metering/visualization. Exact units and valid ranges are not specified.
requirements: position and channel must be within valid bounds for the current buffer/audio frame; specific constraints are not provided.

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::stopPlaying

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::hasSongHalted

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::pausePlaying

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::resumePlaying
functions.description: Resumes playback from paused state.

Return value indicates success or error per implementation.

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::isPaused

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::getPanningSeparation

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::getSongMainVolume

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::getOrder

functions.description: Returns both order and row, useful for synchronization. Precision depends on output latency.

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::getLastUnvisitedPosition

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::getSyncCount
functions.description: Returns the number of rows played since playback start. Useful for synchronization.

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::getSyncSampleCounter

requirements: b true to reset main volume on start, false otherwise.

functions.name: PlayerGeneric::exportToWAV
functions.signature: mp_sint32 PlayerGeneric::exportToWAV(const SYSCHAR* fileName, XModule* module, mp_sint32 startOrder = 0, mp_sint32 endOrder = -1, const mp_ubyte* mutingArray = NULL, mp_uint32 mutingNumChannels = 0, const mp_ubyte* customPanningTable = NULL, AudioDriverBase* preferredDriver = NULL, mp_sint32* timingLUT = NULL, mp_uint32 limiterDrive = 0)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets text string inputs consumed by fuzz stubs using FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# Ensure the script source contains no null bytes. Avoid embedding \x00 anywhere.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,;:+#()[]{}@$^!%&="

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some multi-byte UTF-8 ranges (no NULs)
    s: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.75:
            s.append(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII))
        elif t < 0.9:
            cp = rng.choice(list(range(0x00A1, 0x017F)))
            s.append(chr(cp))
        else:
            cp = rng.choice([0x2603, 0x266B, 0x2764, 0x263A, 0x03A9])
            s.append(chr(cp))
    return ''.join(s)

def _file_exts() -> List[str]:
    return [
        ".xm", ".mod", ".it", ".s3m", ".mtm", ".xmex", ".mdl", ".wav", ".tmp", "",
    ]

def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 120) -> str:
    # Generate plausible paths with directories and extensions
    sep = rng.choice(['/','\\\\'])
    drive = rng.choice(['', rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) + ':'])
    parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        name_len = rng.randint(1, 12)
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, name_len))
    base_len = rng.randint(1, 16)
    base = _rand_ascii(rng, base_len)
    ext = rng.choice(_file_exts())
    path = sep.join([p for p in ([drive] + parts + [base]) if p != '']) + ext
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        prefix = rng.choice(['./', '../', '.\\\\', '..\\\\'])
        path = prefix + path
    if len(path) > max_len:
        path = path[:max_len]
    return path

def _make_corpus_entries(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    entries: List[str] = []

    # Long strings (>=256) for XModule::convertStr preconditions
    entries.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 256))
    entries.append(_rand_utf8(rng, 300))
    entries.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 512))

    # Short and medium strings
    for L in [1, 5, 16, 31, 32, 64, 100, 127, 200]:
        entries.append(_rand_ascii(rng, L))
    entries.extend([
        "MilkyTracker Export",
        "FastTracker II module",
        "ProTracker MOD Export",
        "\tIndented\tTabs\t",
        "Line1\\nLine2\\nLine3",
    ])

    # Filenames/paths
    for _ in range(8):
        entries.append(_rand_filename(rng))
    entries.extend([
        "mod.xm",
        "song.MOD",
        "C:\\temp\\milky\\out.xm",
        "/tmp/milky/out.it",
        "./relative/path/sample.wav",
        "..\\parent\\folder\\test.mtm",
    ])

    # Tracker strings
    entries.extend([
        "Tracker: MilkyPlay/1.0",
        "Tracker: FT2 Compatible",
        "Tracker: IT 2.15",
        _rand_utf8(rng, 40),
    ])

    # Punctuation/symbol-heavy
    entries.append("[Name]_v1.2.3-rc+build@2026")
    entries.append("Artist - Title (Remix) [128BPM]")

    # Exact boundary sizes

    entries.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 257))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    entries = _make_corpus_entries(rng)
    rng.shuffle(entries)

    out = "\n".join(entries)
    enc = out.encode('utf-8')
    if len(enc) > 4096:
        enc = enc[:4096]
        # Backtrack a few bytes to avoid cutting a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence
        for back in range(0, 4):
            try:
                enc[:len(enc)-back].decode('utf-8')
                enc = enc[:len(enc)-back]
                break
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                continue
    return enc

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for filesystem path inputs suitable for XMFile operations.
# Goals:
# - Produce valid, writable file paths within common temp directories.
# - Sometimes point to an existing file with random content (so exists/remove success paths are exercised).
# - Sometimes point to a non-existent path variant (to exercise failure paths).
# - Include a mix of names: simple, nested subdirs, special characters, long names, different extensions.
# - On non-Windows, SYSCHAR == char, so we just return UTF-8 bytes. On Windows this fuzz target casts char* to SYSCHAR*,
#   so avoid wide-only characters; keep ASCII-safe.
# - Keep total buffer <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .()[]{}#@!$%+="

def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 20, ext: str | None = None) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    base = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()
    # Avoid empty or trailing dots/spaces which may be problematic on Windows
    base = base.strip(" .") or "file"
    if ext:
        # ensure ext without dot
        e = ext.lstrip('.')
        return f"{base}.{e}"
    return base

def _ensure_dir(path: str) -> None:
    try:
        os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    except Exception:
        pass

def _maybe_make_existing_file(rng: random.Random, base_dir: str, path: str) -> str:
    # 50% create the file so XMFile::exists can find it. Also sometimes write content.
    make = rng.random() < 0.5
    if not make:
        return path
    try:
        # ensure parent exists
        parent = os.path.dirname(path)
        if parent:
            _ensure_dir(parent)
        # write some random bytes (0..2KB)
        size = rng.randint(0, 2048)
        data = rng.randbytes(size) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))
        with open(path, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(data)
    except Exception:
        # If writing fails (permissions, etc.), just return the path; caller will exercise error paths
        pass
    return path

def _build_path_variants(rng: random.Random, base_dir: str) -> List[str]:
    variants: List[str] = []

    # Simple file in base
    variants.append(os.path.join(base_dir, _rand_name(rng, ext='bin')))

    # Nested subdirectories (1-3 levels)
    depth = rng.randint(1, 3)
    parts = [_rand_name(rng, 3, 12) for _ in range(depth)]
    nested = os.path.join(base_dir, *parts, _rand_name(rng, ext='dat'))
    variants.append(nested)

    # Long filename
    longname = _rand_name(rng, 50, 120, ext='raw')
    variants.append(os.path.join(base_dir, longname))

    # Name with many special characters
    special = ''.join(rng.choice("-_.()[]{}!@#$%^&+=") for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 24)))
    special = (special or "spec").strip(" .") or "spec"
    variants.append(os.path.join(base_dir, f"{special}.tmp"))

    # Hidden-like on POSIX (leading dot)
    variants.append(os.path.join(base_dir, "." + _rand_name(rng, 3, 16)))

    # With spaces
    variants.append(os.path.join(base_dir, _rand_name(rng, 5, 18) + " copy 1.txt"))

    # With subdirs and mixed separators normalized
    subparts = [_rand_name(rng, 2, 10) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4))]
    variants.append(os.path.join(base_dir, *subparts, _rand_name(rng, 4, 12, ext='xm'))
                   )

    # Extremely nested but short names
    deep_parts = ["d" + str(i) for i in range(rng.randint(4, 8))]
    variants.append(os.path.join(base_dir, *deep_parts, _rand_name(rng, 6, 10)))

    # Random extension from common audio/module types
    ext = rng.choice(['xm', 'mod', 's3m', 'it', 'wav', 'mdl', 'ptm'])
    variants.append(os.path.join(base_dir, _rand_name(rng, 4, 16, ext=ext)))

    return variants

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a base directory: prefer system temp; fall back to current directory
    base_dir = os.getenv('TMPDIR') or os.getenv('TEMP') or os.getenv('TMP') or \
               ("C:\\Windows\\Temp" if os.name == 'nt' else "/tmp")

    # Create a fuzzer-specific subdirectory to avoid clutter, ensure it exists
    subdir = f"milky_fuzz_{rng.randint(0, 1_000_000):06d}"
    base = os.path.join(base_dir, subdir)
    _ensure_dir(base)

    # Build a set of candidate paths
    candidates = _build_path_variants(rng, base)

    # Select one
    path = rng.choice(candidates)

    # With some probability create the file to exist already
    path = _maybe_make_existing_file(rng, base, path)

    # Return as bytes (UTF-8)
    s = path
    # Ensure length limit
    if len(s) > 4096:
        s = s[:4096]
    return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
